findings.body: Replacing the batched loadMany with one awaited repo.load per id makes latency and backend load scale linearly with the caller-supplied ids array. There is no size cap, so a large ids list can tie up the handler and hammer the repository. The loop also dereferences item.active without a null check, so a missing id throws.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes thousands of ids. Each is loaded serially, which exhausts request time and database connections and causes a denial of service. Separately, a nonexistent id returns null and item.active throws a TypeError.
findings.title: Avoid unbounded sequential per-id loads (N+1)

expected.label: awaited repository lookup is serialized per ID

findings.anchor: var statement = db.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?");
findings.body: The PreparedStatement is never closed; returning the ResultSet leaves the statement open until the caller closes it (and closing the ResultSet does not close the statement). Under load this exhausts cursors/connections, a resource-exhaustion DoS risk.
findings.failure_scenario: Each call to find opens a statement that is never closed; high request volume exhausts DB cursors, causing ORA-01000/connection failures for all users.
findings.title: Close the PreparedStatement to avoid leaking JDBC resources

findings.body: The query compares `id = ?` exactly, but the bound value is trimmed and lowercased. Any id containing uppercase characters or significant whitespace will not match, depending on column collation. A null userId also throws NullPointerException.
findings.failure_scenario: A call such as find(db, "AbC123") binds "abc123". On a case-sensitive column this returns no rows, so an existing user is reported missing.
findings.title: Don't lowercase/trim the id before an exact-match lookup

findings.body: The 30000 ms default on `timeoutMs` was removed. Callers that omit the argument now get `undefined`. Any consumer that uses this value as a request timeout could then wait indefinitely. This is a resource-safety risk because hung requests can pile up.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller invokes fetchUser(id) without a timeout, so timeoutMs is undefined. Downstream fetch logic applies no timeout, and requests to a slow backend hang and exhaust connections.
findings.title: Restore the default timeout for fetchUser
